heading: client/manifest.json, field by field
body:
The manifest is a standard web app manifest. A browser reads its standard members to install the application. Tachyon reads some of the same members for a native build. It also adds one member of its own, tac, and a browser ignores it. The whole file is public, because the build publishes it at /manifest.webmanifest. Do not put anything private in it. The file is plain JSON: if you compute a value, write the generated client/manifest.json before you run ty bundle. There is no tac.config.js and no tachyon.json, and a top-level tachyon member is refused: a build refuses each one and says where its values moved (ADR 0052).

tac holds two kinds of members. Your own members, such as tac.api.url, are the public configuration that services bind with Settings and Setting (TAC_ names and tac. paths). Tachyon's own members are settings for the build and the native host, not values for services: application, origin, scripts, blockingScripts, styles, styleSources, scriptSources, cache, metadata, sitemap, browserApis, nativeCapabilities, elements, python, budgets, outgoing, go, dotnet, implicitmembers, simplify, accessibility and the check switches below. Do not bind them in a service.

A web build reads the members it needs: scripts, blockingScripts and styles with their sources, cache rules, metadata, the origin, the sitemap, browserApis, outgoing hosts, budgets and python. `browserApis` lists the browser APIs that need the user's consent and that the services may use: any of `clipboard`, `share`, `notifications`, `geolocation` and `preferenceStrings`, each once, for example `"browserApis": ["clipboard", "geolocation"]`. Any other name stops the build (`TY1601`). The page refuses an API that is not listed. `nativeCapabilities` grants native capabilities separately: `["filePicker"]` is the only name today, and without it the file picker answers denied (see the feature Inject an OS file picker into a service). `outgoing.hosts` lists the other hosts that page code may send requests to; the page's `connect-src` allows only these, and the build refuses a request URL with any other host (`TY1326`). Each `scripts` entry is a deferred module that runs after the Tac runtime. Each `blockingScripts` entry is a classic script placed before the runtime, so it runs before the first paint, for example to apply a saved theme; the page waits for it, so keep it small and free of `import` and `export`. A native build takes its name, entry route, identifier, version, window and menus from this file only. `tac.application.menus` adds your own items to the File, View and Help menus of a macOS, Linux or Windows app; iOS and Android refuse it (`TY1601`; see Native menus). `tac.application.window.titleBar: "integrated"` draws the page under the macOS title bar, and `titleBarButtonInset` moves the window buttons (see Window controls).

These `check` settings each turn one build rule off while you migrate, for Tac code only: `tac.cohesion.check`, `tac.duplication.check`, `tac.dependencies.check`, `tac.names.check`, `tac.signatures.check`, `tac.constants.check`, `tac.visibility.check`, `tac.types.check` and `tac.tests.check`, each `false` (`tac.types.check` is off until you set it to `true`; see Cohesive services, Utilities, Dependencies point down, Plain-English names, Small signatures, Named values, Public only when used, Types in every language and Test units). `tac.accessibility.check: false` turns off the accessible-view check (`TY1336`, see Templates). `tac.budgets.script` and `tac.budgets.webassembly` set the size budget of every route in kilobytes (defaults 200 and 3584; without `tac.budgets.script`, a route that loads more than one web runtime gets a measured allowance for each runtime after the largest one), and `tac.budgets.check: false` turns that check off (`TY1337`, see Route size budgets). With `tac.python` and no `tac.budgets.script`, a route that uses a Python service gets a 512 KiB script budget. `tac.elements` lists the components that the build also exports as custom elements, such as `"elements": ["shop-counter"]`; a name without a hyphen or a name that is not a component stops the build (`TY1358`, see Components in other apps). `tac.simplify.suggest` set to `false` hides the simpler-form suggestions for Tac code, and `tac.implicitmembers.suggest` set to `true` shows the receiver suggestions too (off by default; see Simpler forms). `tac.names.words` lists words of your domain, such as a product name, that Tac names may use. `tac.go.compiler` chooses the Go compiler for Go web services: `"tinygo"` or `"go"`; without it a release build tries TinyGo first and falls back to Go (see WebAssembly compilers per language). `tac.dotnet.aot: true` compiles C# and F# web services ahead of time in a release build: faster for heavy computing, but a larger download.

`tac.application.rust` declares crates and helper executables for the Rust companion of a macOS, Linux or Windows app. Its `dependencies` and `platformDependencies` use exact Cargo versions, with optional `features` and `defaultFeatures`; platform keys are `macos`, `linux` and `windows`. Its `executables` maps up to eight program names to Rust class files under `client/`. A packaged desktop build compiles from the project's `vendor/rust/` folder offline and places each helper beside the app executable. The declaration needs a Rust service and does not add crate dependencies to a WebAssembly service. See Rust crates and helper executables under Native services.
